clue.text: Certain muscles shown by ill- disciplined lout close to home

parts.note: abs is the short form of abdominal muscles

indicators.note: badly behaved letters are out of order, so these four are rearranged
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A badly behaved yob shows off his six-pack near his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill- disciplined' rearranges LOUT into OLUT; 'close to' takes the E that ends 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives meaning sure or beyond doubt, as in an absolute certainty.

clue.text: Tincture in a car getting spilt

indicators.note: things spilt are scattered, so the letters of these three words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spills a medicinal tincture inside their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting spilt' rearranges the letters of 'in a car'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal remedy often prepared as a tincture for bruises, so the general word names an example.

clue.text: Trim tree

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance
a coniferous evergreen of the pine family

explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and tidy as an adjective, and it is also the name of a conifer.

clue.text: Latin priest in Tibet getting animal

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk or priest in Tibet

explanation.surface: A Latin-speaking priest in Tibet acquires a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American beast of burden, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Day among volunteers and staff for tiny creature

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a staff is a long stick or pole

explanation.surface: A day spent among volunteers and staff in aid of some little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the small larva of a frog or toad, so it fits a small living thing.

clue.text: Strongly criticise a ship facing trouble

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a vessel heading into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them, here in words, which matches harsh criticism.

clue.text: Newer cost disputed for vegetable

indicators.note: something disputed is contested and thrown into question, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's latest price rise is challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputed' rearranges the nine letters of 'Newer cost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize eaten as a vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: A friend accepting new worker of a bountiful nature

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the friend holds the new letter

parts.note: bud is informal for a pal
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A pal welcomes a generous new employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful and bountiful are close synonyms describing supply in large quantity.

clue.text: Liberal president once restraining priest before Republican? That's more probable

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the priest is held inside

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, a former US president
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A political tale: a liberal ex-president keeps a cleric in check ahead of a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of likely: something likelier has a better chance of happening.

clue.text: Two boys in French region

parts.note: Norm, short for Norman, is a boy's name
Andy is a second boy's name

explanation.surface: A pair of lads find themselves somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region on the northern coast of France.

clue.text: Ridicule half of side — rubbish

indicators.note: only half of the four-letter word is taken, here its second pair

parts.note: bunk means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone mocks half the team as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes DE, the back half of 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk an idea is to expose it as false, which mocks or ridicules it.

clue.text: Barney's covering for leg

definitions.meaning: barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel
a short cloth gaiter worn over the instep and ankle

explanation.walkthrough: Barney is British slang for a row; it is not a man's name here.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, and spats are also old-fashioned gaiters covering the ankle.

clue.text: In high spirits, give bird a ring

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully telephones their feathered friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a ring' reads as phoning, but the ring is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop means jubilant or elated, a straight idiom for being in a buoyant mood.

clue.text: Some fetid algae — typical of the sea?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Smelly seaweed is the kind of thing you find at the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the rise and fall of the ocean, so the adjective describes something characteristic of it.

clue.text: Confused state produced by grain, we hear

indicators.note: says the grain word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: maize is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Bewilderment caused by a cereal, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a maze is to be bewildered, an old sense of the word meaning confusion.

clue.text: Foreign inhabitant and government stopping a payment in Spain

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the government letter fills the payment

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: An expat in Spain finds the state blocking a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argentine is a native or citizen of Argentina, a foreigner from a British point of view.

clue.text: Recount possibly beat in a dominant fashion

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A vote recount might decide who won by a landslide.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat decisively, a thrashing synonym.

clue.text: Careless promotion for artist occupied by melancholy piece of portraiture

indicators.note: in a down clue a promotion lifts the letters upwards, so they read bottom to top
an occupied place has someone inside, so the artist holds the other pieces

parts.note: Frans Hals was a Dutch portrait painter
melancholy means sad

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sloppy advert for a painter, filled with a gloomy bit of portrait work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' looks like advertising, but in a down entry it means reading the built letters upwards; 'occupied by' signals the insertion. Frans Hals painted portraits, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means done hastily and without care, a synonym.

clue.text: Shifting fellow with team recalled as expedient

parts.note: quick can mean moving, as in quicksand that shifts

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the team letters run backwards

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A restless chap and his recalled squad make a stopgap solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick fix is a temporary remedy, and an expedient is a makeshift measure of the same kind.

clue.text: Animal reared in unusual role getting place to sit?

indicators.note: says the reared animal sits inside the rearranged letters
unusual means out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged
reared means raised up, and in an across entry that reads the animal backwards

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

explanation.surface: A beast brought up in an odd part finds somewhere to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ROLE into LOER; 'reared' turns GNU into UNG, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining chair, so the question mark marks a fair example.

clue.text: Hard confection in style of music

definitions.meaning: a stick of hard sugar candy sold at British seaside resorts
a genre of loud guitar-based popular music

explanation.definitionFit: Rock is the stick of seaside candy, and also a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Curse judge elected by vote

parts.note: a candidate elected is in
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A judge, once voted into office, is cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a spell of bad luck, much like a hex or a malediction.

clue.text: Evil criminal in first month producing projectile

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters sit inside the month

parts.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked crook in January produces a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges EVIL into VELI, placed 'in' JAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin is a spear thrown in athletics, an example of a projectile.

clue.text: Old man with part in a conditional release?

parts.note: old man is informal for father, or pa
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Father lands an acting part as early release from jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is a prisoner's early release on condition of good behaviour.

clue.text: Notice surprised expression around lecturer of decent character

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the lecturer letter

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A note reacts with astonishment at a lecturer's decency.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper and in good taste, which fits behaviour of decent character.

clue.text: Exotic canape lacking a nut

indicators.note: exotic means unusual and foreign, so the letters are mixed
lacking says one letter is taken away from those letters before the mix

explanation.surface: An unusual party snack without a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an A ('lacking') from CANAPE and rearrange ('Exotic') CNAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American nut, a specific example of the class.

clue.text: Sparkling drink left by young recruit short of time in procession

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a cadet is a young trainee in the services

explanation.surface: Fizz left behind by a raw recruit running late for a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a formal parade of riders or vehicles, a synonym.

clue.text: Relief gained by eastern European heard on horseback

indicators.note: says the word for a Latvian is said out loud and spelt with one T

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
a rider is said to be up

explanation.surface: A Latvian on a horse brings some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A letup is a pause or lessening, which offers relief.

clue.text: Mention of a food business

indicators.note: mentioning is saying out loud, so the phrase is spoken

parts.note: fare is food, so the words say a fare

explanation.surface: Talking about a meal-related enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in business affairs.

clue.text: Aims of party in part of station?

definitions.meaning: a political party's set of declared policies
the raised area beside the track where passengers board trains

explanation.definitionFit: A platform is a political manifesto and also the raised boarding area at a railway station.

clue.text: Actress right to kiss old novelist

indicators.note: R to X means the right letter is changed into the kiss letter

parts.note: Elizabeth Hurley is an English actress

explanation.surface: An actress has the right to kiss an elderly writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to kiss' means change R into X in HURLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley, author of Brave New World, is a novelist of the past.

clue.text: Trivial pen captivating little boy largely

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the pen encloses the boy

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a nipper is a small child

explanation.surface: A minor writing tool charms a small lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippety means made of scraps or fragments, hence petty and of little importance.
